en: The stiff midrib of a coconut frond acts as a lever to pry open the hard shell of a mature coconut.
Natural rocky slopes on Mayon Volcano act as inclined planes, allowing volcanic debris to slide down gradually.
The wide hooves of a carabao increase friction and distribute weight to prevent sinking in muddy rice paddies.
Earth's gravity pulls rainwater from the Cordillera mountains down through the cascading levels of the Banaue Rice Terraces.
Black sand beaches in Zambales contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic iron mineral that sticks to lodestones.
During the Habagat monsoon, friction between ice particles in storm clouds generates the static electricity released as lightning.
Fireflies in the mangroves of Palawan produce visible light through a chemical reaction called bioluminescence to attract mates.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River produces distinct echoes because sound waves bounce off its massive limestone cave walls.
Geysers in the Tiwi geothermal field in Albay are heated by hot magma located deep beneath the Earth's crust.
A falling mature coconut converts gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy as it drops from the tall palm tree.
Thermal energy from the hot springs of Los Baños transfers to the cooler surrounding soil through direct conduction.
Abaca plants in Catanduananes transform light energy from the sun into chemical energy stored within their strong leaf fibers.
